This
document lists the equipment Inspection checklist I1,
which must be performed on a daily bases as indicated by D1 in the title block
for all HETACHI energized transformers by operation staff.

items:
Don't
 go too close to energized areas on the transformer while it is operating too
 close, means as a general understanding within a spherical area whose center
 is the top of the bushing and whose radius is the full length from the top
 of the bushing flange (ground potential) of the bushing.

Read
 and record oil and winding temperature, check that the maximum
 temperatures are not being exceeded, also check that the temperature is
 acceptable by comparing it with past entries in the inspection log.

Voltages
 and load must be kept within the specified limits, which are in the
 instruction manual.

Read
 and record the values on the oil level gauges, check that the oil level
 readings are correct for the oil temperature, in compliance with the graph
 on the nameplate located near them, (in nameplate) and this graph also
 appears in the transformers instruction manual.

sections.text:
Audible
 Noise And Loosely Bolted Parts

items:
Listen and check for any abnormal sounds from the main tank and 
accessories as a rattling sound indicates loose bolts and a
 repetitive scraping sound indicates worn fan or oil pump bearings.

Visually
 inspect bolted connections in the transformer's main and auxiliary circuits,
 foundation bolts and all other bolted connections to ensure that all parts
 are secure.

Check that none of the valves is loose, such as the oil 
 inlet and out let valves. For valve condition, refer to oil piping diagram 
 in the instruction manual.

Check
 for leakage from the transformer tank, valves, pipes, gauges, gasket joints
 welds etc.

The
 silica-gel absorbent inside the breather bottle is normally magenta blue,
 but turns pink if excessive moisture is present, dry or replace the silica
 gel if more than 70% is pink.

Check
 that the sight-glass level of the sealing oil in the oil cup is between
 the HIGH and LOW marks, it must be correct at all times because excessive
 sealing oil in the cup may contaminate the silica-gel, while a shortage of
 oil may not seal the conservator properly.

Check
 for cracks, oil or gas leakage or any sign of damage to the pressure plate.

On
 forced oil cooled and forced oil/forced air-cooled transformers, check for
 abnormal rotation related sounds and vibrations.

Check
 for an excessive buildup of grime on the radiator surface and remove it.

Check
 that any oil flow indicator installed in the system shows that oil is
 circulating.

Check
 that radiator valves are in the open position.

Make
 sure no oil is leaking from the main tank into the OLTC by checking that
 the OLTC conservator oil level is not too high. If the oil level is too
 high, oil may be seeping through the insulating cylinder of the diverted
 switch compartment, if this compartment is leaking the escaping
 contaminated oil may seriously affect the transformer's insulation
 specifications, leading to internal arcing.

Check
 the level of oil in the gearbox , it should be up to the red mark, usually
 oil needs to be supplied every 3 to 6 months, use turbine oil SAE 20 W120.

Check
 for any abnormal sounds or vibrations during operation.

Check
 that the stop position indicator is positioned within the safety zone
 (usually marked green).

Record
 the number of tap changing operations and check that the operations
 counter functions correctly.

If
 the bushings are equipped with an oil gauge, use binoculars to visually
 check the oil level and for signs of leakage.

Check
 the porcelain for cracking and other damage.

Check
 that there is no overheating of the terminals, inspect the terminals for
 heat discoloration using binoculars or infra red scope.

Check
 the pressure of N2 gas, the gauge pointer should not be in red range and
 if the gauge pointer is in red range, gas shall be refilled up to 0.2
 kg/cm2.

Check the transformer's protective relays at the site control room 
 and check that they have not actuated.

Open
 the conservator drain valve about once every 3 months to drain off any water condensation.

Substations | Technical Procedure
This
document lists the equipment Inspection checklist I1,
which must be performed on a daily bases as indicated by D1 in the title block
for all HETACHI energized transformers by operation staff.
Safety
Precautions
Don't
 go too close to energized areas on the transformer while it is operating too
 close, means as a general understanding within a spherical area whose center
 is the top of the bushing and whose radius is the full length from the top
 of the bushing flange (ground potential) of the bushing.
Work to be carried out
Transformer Temperatures, Load And Voltages
Read
 and record oil and winding temperature, check that the maximum
 temperatures are not being exceeded, also check that the temperature is
 acceptable by comparing it with past entries in the inspection log.
Voltages
 and load must be kept within the specified limits, which are in the
 instruction manual.
Oil
 Level
Read
 and record the values on the oil level gauges, check that the oil level
 readings are correct for the oil temperature, in compliance with the graph
 on the nameplate located near them, (in nameplate) and this graph also
 appears in the transformers instruction manual.
Audible
 Noise And Loosely Bolted Parts
Listen and check for any abnormal sounds from the main tank and 
accessories as a rattling sound indicates loose bolts and a
 repetitive scraping sound indicates worn fan or oil pump bearings.
Loosely
 Bolted Parts
Visually
 inspect bolted connections in the transformer's main and auxiliary circuits,
 foundation bolts and all other bolted connections to ensure that all parts
 are secure.
Check that none of the valves is loose, such as the oil 
 inlet and out let valves. For valve condition, refer to oil piping diagram 
 in the instruction manual.
Oil
 Leakage
Check
 for leakage from the transformer tank, valves, pipes, gauges, gasket joints
 welds etc.
The
 silica-gel absorbent inside the breather bottle is normally magenta blue,
 but turns pink if excessive moisture is present, dry or replace the silica
 gel if more than 70% is pink.
Check
 that the sight-glass level of the sealing oil in the oil cup is between
 the HIGH and LOW marks, it must be correct at all times because excessive
 sealing oil in the cup may contaminate the silica-gel, while a shortage of
 oil may not seal the conservator properly.
Pressure
 Relief Device
Check
 for cracks, oil or gas leakage or any sign of damage to the pressure plate.
Cooling
 Equipment
On
 forced oil cooled and forced oil/forced air-cooled transformers, check for
 abnormal rotation related sounds and vibrations.
Check
 for an excessive buildup of grime on the radiator surface and remove it.
Check
 that any oil flow indicator installed in the system shows that oil is
 circulating.
Check
 that radiator valves are in the open position.
On
Load Tap Changer (OLTC)
Make
 sure no oil is leaking from the main tank into the OLTC by checking that
 the OLTC conservator oil level is not too high. If the oil level is too
 high, oil may be seeping through the insulating cylinder of the diverted
 switch compartment, if this compartment is leaking the escaping
 contaminated oil may seriously affect the transformer's insulation
 specifications, leading to internal arcing.
Check
 the level of oil in the gearbox , it should be up to the red mark, usually
 oil needs to be supplied every 3 to 6 months, use turbine oil SAE 20 W120.
Check
 for any abnormal sounds or vibrations during operation.
Check
 that the stop position indicator is positioned within the safety zone
 (usually marked green).
Record
 the number of tap changing operations and check that the operations
 counter functions correctly.
If
 the bushings are equipped with an oil gauge, use binoculars to visually
 check the oil level and for signs of leakage.
Check
 the porcelain for cracking and other damage.
Check
 that there is no overheating of the terminals, inspect the terminals for
 heat discoloration using binoculars or infra red scope.
Check
 the pressure of N2 gas, the gauge pointer should not be in red range and
 if the gauge pointer is in red range, gas shall be refilled up to 0.2
 kg/cm2.
Check the transformer's protective relays at the site control room 
 and check that they have not actuated.
Open
 the conservator drain valve about once every 3 months to drain off any water condensation.
